q1.where: Stage 1, first part: split in the lip and gum on the left

q2.answer: In the bone under the pink gum, the bone that holds the teeth, from the floor of the nose down to the gum.
q2.where: Stage 1 (gap in the bone) and Stage 2

q3.answer: The small tooth next to the left front tooth never grew. About half of children with a cleft do not have it.

q4.answer: The eye tooth waits high in the bone and needs bone to grow into, so the graft gives it bone to come down into.

q7.answer: New bone fills the gap from the floor of the nose to the gum, it joins the two parts of the upper jaw, and the gum has healed over it. The eye tooth is still in the bone but starts moving down toward the new bone.

q8.answer: With an X-ray at about 3 to 6 months, to see how well the new bone has taken.

q9.answer: The hip can be sore for a while after surgery.

q10.answer: It has come down through the new bone into the row of teeth. Some get stuck and need a small operation.

q12.answer: Braces move the eye tooth into the gap and the dentist reshapes it; or keep the gap with a false tooth on a plate you can take out; or, when you stop growing, an implant or a bridge. The cleft team helps you choose.
